Introduction 1.1 Purpose This document is the comprehensive program document for the Loan Against Mutual Funds (LAMF) product offered by Shriram Credit Company Limited (SCCL). It consolidates the product definition, credit policy, customer journey, system configuration requirements, process ownership matrix, regulatory and compliance framework, risk management approach, fund flow mechanics, profitability framework, partnership model, and governance structure into a single authoritative reference. This document is intended for use by the Product, Credit, Risk, Compliance, Technology, Operations, and Finance teams at SCCL. 1.2 Background SCCL offers LAMF as part of its Loan Against Securities (LAS) product suite. LAMF enables investors holding mutual fund units to access secured credit without liquidating their investments. The product is offered as Single or Multiple Disbursement facility basis Sanction Limit, backed by a

investors holding mutual fund units to access secured credit without liquidating their investments. The product is offered as Single or Multiple Disbursement facility basis Sanction Limit, backed by a pledge of eligible mutual fund units registered with and managed through MF Central. Once the Sanction limit is activated, the customer can draw funds up to the approved Drawing Power limit in one or more tranches. Repayment of the utilised balance is collected under one of two configurations set at sanction: EMI or Balloon: both operating within the Sanctioned Limit structure. Currently only Balloon repayment is offered. SCCL's LAMF program is operated on LOS & platform hosted in our cloud: LOS for loan origination and LMS for loan management and servicing. The product currently supports direct digital origination via the SCCL Website and we are also creating provision for partner-enabled origination via API integrations with third-party platforms and Group employee through HRMS. 1.3 Scope Product structure, parameters, and pricing framework. Credit policy, eligibility criteria, and bureau evaluation rules. End-to-end customer journey from identity verification to withdrawal. LOS

Loan servicing: repayment, appropriation logic, part payment, collections. Collateral monitoring: LTV, Drawing Power, Risk Comfort, margin call, invoke/revoke. Partnership and distribution model including partner commercials. Exception and approval matrix. Under the dynamic model, the applicable interest rate will fall within the range of 9.5% to 15% per annum, determined at origination based on the following three parameters: Sanctioned Limit Credit Score Mutual Fund type (Equity/Debt) Rate once sanctioned is fixed for the loan tenure and is not revised mid-tenure. For LSP / partner-sourced loans, the base rate is defined by both LSP & RE in an agreement. 2.3 Repayment Structures LAMF at SCCL is offered as Single or Multiple Disbursement facility. Repayment of the utilised balance is collected under one of two configurations (EMI or Balloon) set at the time of sanction. Collateral Management and Monitoring 11.1 Sanction Limit Calculation Sanction Limit is the maximum amount a borrower may withdraw at any point. Sanction Limit = eligible collateral value x applicable LTV. Equity: 45%. Debt: 75%. Sanction Limit is recalculated every day following NAV refresh from MF Central API. For all lien marked schemes in LMS are updated with the current market value through Value Research API. 11.2 Risk Comfort Metrics SCCL tracks the following collateral coverage metrics in LMS for each active LAMF account: Risk Comfort % = (Total Loan Outstanding / Latest Collateral Value) x 100. Measures current exposure against market value of pledged collateral. Qualified Loan Amount = Sum of (LTV x Current Market Value) across all lien-marked schemes. Equity: 45%. Debt: 75%. Derived Risk Comfort % = (Qualified Loan Amount / Total

value of pledged collateral. Qualified Loan Amount = Sum of (LTV x Current Market Value) across all lien-marked schemes. Equity: 45%. Debt: 75%. Derived Risk Comfort % = (Qualified Loan Amount / Total Loan Outstanding) x 100. Amount of Breach = Total Loan Outstanding Minus Qualified Loan Amount. Displayed as 0 if positive (no breach). Displayed as absolute value if negative (breach exists). Days Past Breach Count begins from the date Risk Comfort Breach is first set to 'Yes'. Resets if breach is cured and then reoccurs. Derived Risk Comfort % is monitored across five buckets in LMS: below 90%; 85%–90%; 80%–85%; 75%–80%; below 75%. Accounts in the below 75% bucket require immediate review and margin call action. 11.3 LTV Breach and Margin Call Procedure When the Risk Comfort breach flag is set to 'Yes' (Amount of Breach is negative), the following sequence of actions is initiated: LMS detects the breach via daily Sanction limit recalculation.
